title: The Boiling Pot and Ezekiel's Wife Dies

questions.question: On what precise date did the word of the Lord come to Ezekiel, commanding him to write down the name of this day?
options: In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month
In the fifth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day
In the thirtieth year, on the first day of the month
In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month
questions.correctAnswer: In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:1-2 (ESV): "In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me: 'Son of man, write down the name of this day, this very day.'"

questions.question: What significant event happened on "this very day" that Ezekiel was to write down?
options: The king of Babylon had laid siege to Jerusalem
The temple was burned to the ground
Zedekiah was captured and blinded
The false prophet Hananiah died
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Babylon had laid siege to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:2 (ESV): "The king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem this very day."

questions.question: What parable is Ezekiel told to utter to the rebellious house regarding a cooking vessel?
options: "Set on the pot, set it on, pour in water also; put in it the pieces of meat..."
"Break the clay jar before the elders of the city..."
"Fill the vessel with oil and pour it upon the altar..."
"Wash the cup thoroughly, yet it remains dirty on the inside..."
questions.correctAnswer: "Set on the pot, set it on, pour in water also; put in it the pieces of meat..."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:3-4 (ESV): "utter a parable to the rebellious house... Set on the pot, set it on, pour in water also; put in it the pieces of meat,"

questions.question: What does the bloody city of Jerusalem resemble in the parable of the pot?
options: A pot whose rust is in it, and whose rust has not gone out of it
A pot made of cracked clay that holds no water
A golden bowl filled with abominations
A boiling cauldron that tips toward the north
questions.correctAnswer: A pot whose rust is in it, and whose rust has not gone out of it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:6 (ESV): "Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose rust is in it, and whose rust has not gone out of it!"

questions.question: Where did the bloody city pour out her blood?
options: On the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with earth
In the holy of holies where no one could see it
Into the river Kidron so it would flow away
In the valley of Hinnom
questions.correctAnswer: On the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with earth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:7 (ESV): "For the blood she has shed is in her midst; she put it on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with earth."

questions.question: What does God command to be done to the pot after the meat is boiled and removed, to cleanse it of its rust?
options: Set it empty upon the coals, that it may become hot, and its copper may burn... that its rust may be consumed
Smash it into pieces and throw the pieces into the valley
Bury it in the earth for forty days
Wash it with strong lye and water in the river
questions.correctAnswer: Set it empty upon the coals, that it may become hot, and its copper may burn... that its rust may be consumed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:11 (ESV): "Then set it empty upon the coals, that it may become hot, and its copper may burn, that its uncleanness may be melted in it, its rust consumed."

questions.question: God tells Ezekiel He is about to take away "the delight of your eyes" with a single fatal stroke. Who was this?
options: Ezekiel's wife
His firstborn son
The template in Jerusalem
His remaining sight
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16, 18 (ESV): "Son of man, behold, I am about to take the delight of your eyes away from you at a stroke... And in the evening my wife died."

questions.question: What was Ezekiel explicitly commanded NOT to do when the delight of his eyes was taken?
options: He was not to mourn, weep, or let his tears run down; he must not make any mourning for the dead
He was not to leave his house for seven days
He was not to tell anyone she died until they noticed
He was not to bury her in the land of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: He was not to mourn, weep, or let his tears run down; he must not make any mourning for the dead
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16-17 (ESV): "yet you shall not mourn or weep, nor shall your tears run down. Sigh, but not aloud; make no mourning for the dead."

questions.question: What normal mourning customs was Ezekiel forbidden from doing?
options: Binding on his turban, putting shoes on his feet, covering his lips, or eating the bread of mourners
Tearing his clothes and cutting his hair
Washing his face and anointing himself with oil
Fasting and sleeping on the floor
questions.correctAnswer: Binding on his turban, putting shoes on his feet, covering his lips, or eating the bread of mourners
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:17 (ESV): "Bind on your turban, and put your shoes on your feet; do not cover your lips, nor eat the bread of mourners." (He was told to do the opposite of standard mourning—wear the turban, wear shoes, don't cover lips).

questions.question: When Ezekiel did as commanded the morning after his wife died, what did the people ask him?
options: "Will you not tell us what these things mean for us, that you are acting thus?"
"Why are you disrespecting the dead?"
"Has the Lord spoken to you in a dream?"
"Shall we also cease from mourning our dead?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Will you not tell us what these things mean for us, that you are acting thus?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:19 (ESV): "And the people said to me, 'Will you not tell us what these things mean for us, that you are acting thus?'"

questions.question: What did Ezekiel say God was about to profane, which was "the delight of *their* eyes"?
options: His sanctuary, the pride of their power, the delight of their eyes
The throne of David
The city walls of Jerusalem
The ark of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: His sanctuary, the pride of their power, the delight of their eyes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:21 (ESV): "Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your power, the delight of your eyes, and the yearning of your soul;"

questions.question: What will the people do when the sanctuary is destroyed and their sons and daughters fall by the sword?
options: They shall do as Ezekiel had done: they shall not mourn or weep, but pine away in their iniquities
They will tear their clothes in the streets of Babylon
They will rebel against their captors
They will finally repent and sing songs of deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: They shall do as Ezekiel had done: they shall not mourn or weep, but pine away in their iniquities
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:22-23 (ESV): "And you shall do as I have done... You shall not mourn or weep, but you shall pine away in your iniquities and groan to one another."

questions.question: What is the "sign" provided to the people through Ezekiel's actions?
options: "Ezekiel shall be to you a sign; according to all that he has done you shall do. When this comes, then you will know that I am the Lord God."
"A rainbow in the sky after the storm."
"The pot boiling over the coals until it is consumed."
"A broken staff left in the dust."
questions.correctAnswer: "Ezekiel shall be to you a sign; according to all that he has done you shall do. When this comes, then you will know that I am the Lord God."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:24 (ESV): "Thus shall Ezekiel be to you a sign; according to all that he has done you shall do. When this comes, then you will know that I am the Lord God."

questions.question: What will happen on the day God takes from them their stronghold and the delight of their eyes?
options: A fugitive will come to Ezekiel to report the news to him
The sky will turn dark at noon
An eagle will drop a branch on Ezekiel's roof
All the exiles will return home
questions.correctAnswer: A fugitive will come to Ezekiel to report the news to him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:25-26 (ESV): "on that day, a fugitive will come to you to report to you the news."

questions.question: What specifically will happen to Ezekiel's own condition on the day the fugitive arrives?
options: His mouth will be opened; he shall speak and be no longer mute
He will be struck blind
He will weep for the first time since his wife died
He will be taken up into heaven in a whirlwind
questions.correctAnswer: His mouth will be opened; he shall speak and be no longer mute
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:27 (ESV): "On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive, and you shall speak and be no longer mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the Lord."

key_verse_text: "Thus shall Ezekiel be to you a sign; according to all that he has done you shall do. When this comes, then you will know that I am the Lord God."
